# =============================================================================
# Harmonia Experiment Failure Mode Taxonomy
# =============================================================================
# Schema version: 1.2
# Date: 26 February 2026 (added 6A: Kernel State Budget Enforced)
#
# This file defines the problem classes that the CLI log/trace analysis tool
# uses to categorize experiment failures. Each problem class has:
#   - id: unique identifier (category_number + letter)
#   - category: high-level grouping
#   - name: short descriptive name
#   - description: full explanation
#   - severity: critical | error | warning | info
#   - detection: keyword/regex patterns to search for in logs and traces
#   - example: real snippet from a log or trace
#   - remediation: list of suggested fixes
#
# COMPOUND DETECTION LOGIC:
# Some problem classes require compound conditions (e.g., "all turns timeout
# AND raw_messages count <= 1 per turn"). These cannot be expressed as simple
# keyword/regex patterns. They are implemented in Python in the CLI tool
# (see _detect_* methods). This YAML only contains the simple patterns;
# compound logic is documented in comments under each relevant problem class.
#
# See also: documentation/processes/11_02_2026_interpreting_logs_and_traces.md
# =============================================================================

schema_version: "1.2"

problem_classes:

  # ===========================================================================
  # Category 1: Infrastructure / Beaker Server Failures
  # ===========================================================================

  - id: "1A"
    category: "infrastructure"
    name: "Beaker Server Hung"
    description: |
      The Beaker server becomes unresponsive after processing a previous batch
      of experiment runs. All 8 turns timeout with an identical, deterministic
      duration pattern [180, 300, 180, 180, 360, 600, 300, 120] totaling exactly
      2220 seconds. Each turn's raw_messages contains only a single status:busy
      message — the Beaker kernel never starts processing.
    severity: "critical"
    detection:
      # COMPOUND LOGIC (implemented in Python as _detect_beaker_server_hung):
      #   1. ALL turns have response_type == "timeout"
      #   2. Each turn has <= 1 raw_message
      #   3. Total duration is approximately 2220 seconds (± 30s)
      # These conditions together distinguish infrastructure hang from
      # LLM-side timeouts (3A), where raw_messages count > 1 per turn.
      log_keywords: []
      log_regex: []
      # 1A detection is PURELY compound (Python-only). No simple keywords,
      # because "Request timed out after" also appears in 3A (LLM-side timeout).
      trace_keywords: []
      trace_regex: []
    example:
      source: "trace"
      snippet: |
        {
          "turn": 1,
          "agent_response": "Request timed out after 180.0 seconds",
          "response_type": "timeout",
          "tool_calls": [],
          "duration_seconds": 180.001,
          "raw_messages": [
            {
              "msg_type": "status",
              "content": { "execution_state": "busy" }
            }
          ]
        }
    remediation:
      - "Restart Beaker between runs: modify run_experiment.py to restart the Beaker server (or kernel) between experiment runs"
      - "Detect hung server: send a health-check request (GET /api/sessions) before sending turns; abort if no response within 10s"
      - "Limit retries: only attempt one run per Beaker server instance, or restart server between retries"

  - id: "1B"
    category: "infrastructure"
    name: "405 Method Not Allowed on Notebook Save"
    description: |
      Beaker returns HTTP 405 when attempting to save a notebook. This appears
      in almost all SLURM .out logs as a warning but does not crash the experiment.
      Beaker's dev mode tries to auto-save notebooks, but the API doesn't support
      PUT for this path.
    severity: "info"
    detection:
      log_keywords:
        - "405 PUT /api/contents/notebook.ipynb"
      log_regex:
        - "\\d+ PUT /api/contents/.*\\.ipynb"
      trace_keywords: []
      trace_regex: []
    example:
      source: "log"
      snippet: |
        [W 2026-02-10 19:34:33.506 BeakerServerApp] 405 PUT /api/contents/notebook.ipynb (::1) 0.74ms referer=None
    remediation:
      - "Ignore: this is a non-fatal warning that does not affect experiment results"
      - "Suppress in logging: configure Beaker's logging level to suppress 405 warnings"
      - "Fix Beaker config: configure the correct save endpoint if notebook saving is desired"

  - id: "1C"
    category: "infrastructure"
    name: "ZMQ ReadTimeout on Context Cleanup"
    description: |
      After the experiment completes, the Beaker kernel's cleanup process
      encounters a ZMQ ReadTimeout when trying to tear down the context.
      This appears in the SLURM .out log at the very end and does not affect
      experiment results.
    severity: "info"
    detection:
      log_keywords:
        - "Uncaught exception in ZMQStream callback"
        - "zmq.error.ZMQError"
      log_regex:
        - "ZMQ.*[Tt]imeout"
        - "Uncaught exception in ZMQStream"
      trace_keywords: []
      trace_regex: []
    example:
      source: "log"
      snippet: |
        Uncaught exception in ZMQStream callback
        Traceback (most recent call last):
          File ".../zmq/eventloop/zmqstream.py", line 565, in _log_error
            f.result()
          File ".../beaker_kernel/lib/jupyter_kernel_proxy.py", line 253, in handler
          ...
          File ".../beaker_kernel/kernel.py", line 550, in llm_request
            result = await task
    remediation:
      - "Ignore: occurs during cleanup after the experiment finishes; does not affect results"
      - "Graceful shutdown: implement a proper shutdown sequence that sends a kernel shutdown request before disconnecting"
      - "Catch and suppress: wrap the Beaker kernel's cleanup handler in try/except"

  # ===========================================================================
  # Category 2: Model Configuration / Availability Errors
  # ===========================================================================

  - id: "2A"
    category: "model_config"
    name: "Ollama Model Not Found"
    description: |
      The Ollama API returns HTTP 404 because the requested model name does not
      match any installed model. The model is either misspelled or not pulled.
    severity: "critical"
    detection:
      log_keywords: []
      log_regex:
        - "model '.*' not found"
        - "ResponseError.*not found.*status code: 404"
      trace_keywords: []
      trace_regex: []
    example:
      source: "log"
      snippet: |
        ollama._types.ResponseError: model 'olmo-3.1:32b' not found (status code: 404)
    remediation:
      - "Fix model name in config YAML to match an installed model; verify with 'ollama list'"
      - "Add model validation to exec_apptainer_harmonia.sh: verify requested model exists after Ollama starts"
      - "Import custom model from HuggingFace GGUF: 'ollama create <name> -f Modelfile'"

  - id: "2B"
    category: "model_config"
    name: "Tool Calling Not Supported"
    description: |
      The LLM framework (Archytas/LangChain) raises a ValueError because the
      model's Ollama template does not declare tool support. Ollama determines
      tool support by checking if the model's Go template references {{ .Tools }}.
      The model may actually support tool calling natively, but the Ollama template
      is missing the required block.
    severity: "critical"
    detection:
      log_keywords:
        - "does not support tool calling"
        - "does not support tool"
      log_regex:
        - "ValueError.*does not support tool"
      trace_keywords: []
      trace_regex: []
    example:
      source: "log"
      snippet: |
        ValueError: Model 'kimi-k2' does not support tool calling
    remediation:
      - "Use community model with tool template: e.g., 'ollama pull huihui_ai/kimi-k2'"
      - "Create custom Modelfile that adds {{ .Tools }} template block"
      - "Check if ValueError comes from Ollama or from Archytas/LangChain pre-checking; add to allowlist if client-side"

  - id: "2C"
    category: "model_config"
    name: "Ollama Runner Process Crash"
    description: |
      The Ollama runner subprocess crashes with exit status 2 during model
      inference. This is an Ollama-internal error, typically related to model
      loading, GGUF format issues, or GPU memory exhaustion.
    severity: "critical"
    detection:
      log_keywords:
        - "llama runner process has terminated"
        - "exit status 2"
      log_regex:
        - "llama runner.*exit status \\d+"
      trace_keywords: []
      trace_regex: []
    example:
      source: "log"
      snippet: |
        llama runner process has terminated: exit status 2
    remediation:
      - "Check model integrity: re-pull the model with 'ollama pull <model>'"
      - "Check GPU memory: use 'seff <jobid>' to check memory usage; try smaller quantization or more VRAM"
      - "Check Ollama version compatibility: some models require newer Ollama versions"

  - id: "2D"
    category: "model_config"
    name: "OpenRouter Model No Longer Available"
    description: |
      The OpenRouter API returns HTTP 404 indicating that a free-tier model's
      free period has ended and the model must be accessed via a paid slug.
      All turns complete in <1 second (the API error is immediate) and
      total experiment duration is typically <10s.
    severity: "critical"
    detection:
      log_keywords: []
      log_regex: []
      trace_keywords:
        - "period has ended"
        - "migrate to the paid slug"
      trace_regex:
        - "free.*period has ended"
        - "migrate to the paid slug"
    example:
      source: "trace"
      snippet: |
        LLM Error:
            Error from OpenRouter: {'error': {'message': 'The free MiMo-V2-Flash period has ended. To continue using this model, please migrate to the paid slug: xiaomi/mimo-v2-flash', 'code': 404}}
    remediation:
      - "Remove from roster: delete the config YAML for models that are no longer free"
      - "Switch to paid slug: update config to use paid model slug with sufficient OpenRouter credits"
      - "Add availability check: make lightweight API call before experiment to verify model is accessible"

  - id: "2E"
    category: "model_config"
    name: "OpenRouter Rate Limit Exceeded"
    description: |
      The OpenRouter API returns HTTP 429 when the free-tier rate limit is
      exceeded. Free models are typically limited to 20 requests/minute.
      First 1-2 turns may succeed, then subsequent turns return empty responses
      very quickly (<1s).
    severity: "error"
    detection:
      log_keywords: []
      log_regex: []
      trace_keywords:
        - "Rate limit exceeded"
        - "rate limit"
      trace_regex:
        - "'code': 429"
        - "Rate limit exceeded.*free-models"
        - "X-RateLimit-Remaining.*0"
    example:
      source: "trace"
      snippet: |
        LLM Error:
            Error from OpenRouter: {'error': {'message': 'Rate limit exceeded: free-models-per-min. ', 'code': 429, 'metadata': {'headers': {'X-RateLimit-Limit': '20', 'X-RateLimit-Remaining': '0'}}}}
    remediation:
      - "Add rate limiting: implement configurable delay between turns (3-5s for free models at 20 req/min)"
      - "Implement retry with backoff: parse X-RateLimit-Reset header and wait before retrying"
      - "Use paid tier: paid OpenRouter plans have significantly higher rate limits"

  - id: "2F"
    category: "model_config"
    name: "Model Pre-load Timeout (Beaker Never Started)"
    description: |
      The Ollama model pre-loading step in exec_apptainer_harmonia.sh exceeds the
      MAX_WAIT timeout (default 300s). The pre-load curl to /api/generate blocks
      while Ollama loads the model into GPU/CPU memory and runs a warm-up inference.
      Beaker never starts because the script is still waiting on the pre-load.
      The sbatch wrapper's readiness poll gives up and kills everything.

      Three root causes observed:
      1. Model saturates GPU VRAM (e.g., 24 GB model on 24 GB GPU) causing
         partial CPU offload and extremely slow loading.
      2. Very large model file (e.g., 31 GB Q8_0) takes too long to read from
         NFS and load into GPU memory, even with sufficient VRAM.
      3. GPU contention: two SLURM GPU jobs land on the same node/GPU, and the
         first model to load consumes all VRAM, starving the second.

      Distinguishing signature: SLURM .out log contains "Pre-loading model: <name>"
      but never "Model preloaded successfully". No results directory is created.
      No trace.json exists. The ollama log shows model loading started but never
      completed.
    severity: "critical"
    detection:
      log_keywords:
        - "Pre-loading model"
      log_regex:
        - "Pre-loading model:.*"
      trace_keywords: []
      trace_regex: []
      # COMPOUND LOGIC (not yet implemented):
      #   1. Log contains "Pre-loading model:" but NOT "Model preloaded successfully"
      #   2. No results directory exists for this run
      #   3. No trace.json found
    example:
      source: "log"
      snippet: |
        GPU 0: Tesla V100-PCIE-16GB (UUID: GPU-...)
        Starting Ollama server on port 11434 ...
        Ollama server is ready
        Pre-loading model: nemotron-3-nano:30b
        [300 seconds pass, no further output]
        Timeout waiting for Beaker to start
    remediation:
      - "Increase MAX_WAIT from 300s to 600s in sbatch template for larger models (30B+ or Q8_0)"
      - "Match model size to GPU VRAM: avoid loading models that saturate available VRAM (leave 2-4 GB headroom)"
      - "Prevent GPU contention: use SLURM --exclusive or --gres=gpu:1 to ensure single-tenant GPU allocation"
      - "Pre-pull models to local scratch before job starts to avoid NFS bottleneck during loading"
      - "Use smaller quantizations (Q4_K_M instead of Q8_0) for models that are borderline for the GPU"

  # ===========================================================================
  # Category 3: LLM Behavioral Failures
  # ===========================================================================

  - id: "3A"
    category: "llm_behavioral"
    name: "LLM-Side Timeout on Complex Tasks"
    description: |
      The LLM responds to simple prompts (data loading, basic questions) but
      stalls/times out on complex analytical tasks (schema matching, value
      mapping). The model is running but takes too long to generate a response.
    severity: "error"
    detection:
      # COMPOUND LOGIC (implemented in Python as _detect_llm_side_timeout):
      #   1. Turn has response_type == "timeout"
      #   2. Turn has > 1 raw_message (differentiates from 1A infrastructure hang)
      #   3. raw_messages include beaker__execute_input or stream messages
      #      (the kernel IS processing, but the LLM is slow)
      #   4. Other turns in the same experiment may have succeeded
      # This distinguishes from 1A where ALL turns timeout with exactly 1
      # raw_message each.
      # 3A detection is PURELY compound (Python-only). No simple keywords,
      # because "Request timed out after" also appears in 1A (Beaker hung).
      # The compound logic checks raw_message count > 1 per timeout turn.
      log_keywords: []
      log_regex: []
      trace_keywords: []
      trace_regex: []
    example:
      source: "trace"
      snippet: |
        Turn 1: response_type=llm_response, duration=16.8s (success)
        Turn 3: response_type=timeout, duration=180.0s, raw_messages=[
          {msg_type: "status", content: {execution_state: "busy"}},
          {msg_type: "beaker__execute_input", ...},
          {msg_type: "stream", ...}
        ]
    remediation:
      - "Increase per-turn timeout from 180s to 600s+ for complex tasks in experiment config"
      - "Simplify prompts: break complex multi-step tasks into smaller, focused turns"
      - "Use faster/larger models: smaller models (<30B) struggle with complex reasoning; try 70B+ or cloud models"

  - id: "3B"
    category: "llm_behavioral"
    name: "LLM Not Using Tools / Text-Only Guidance"
    description: |
      The LLM responds to prompts but does NOT use Beaker's code execution
      capabilities. Instead, it outputs text guidance like "here's the Python
      code you could run" or "I can't directly manipulate files." This defeats
      the purpose of the agent framework.
    severity: "error"
    detection:
      # COMPOUND LOGIC (implemented in Python as _detect_not_using_tools):
      #   1. Turn has response_type == "llm_response" (not timeout)
      #   2. tool_calls array is empty
      #   3. agent_response contains phrases indicating text-only guidance
      # The keyword detection below catches the most common phrases.
      log_keywords: []
      log_regex: []
      trace_keywords:
        - "I don't have the capability"
        - "I can't directly"
        - "here's how you could"
        - "I cannot directly"
        - "you could run"
        - "I'm unable to"
      trace_regex:
        - "(?i)I (?:don't|do not|can't|cannot) (?:have the capability|directly)"
        - "(?i)here'?s (?:how|the code) you could"
    example:
      source: "trace"
      snippet: |
        {
          "turn": 7,
          "agent_response": "I don't have the capability to directly save files to the filesystem. However, I can guide you through the process...",
          "response_type": "llm_response",
          "tool_calls": [],
          "duration_seconds": 17.0
        }
    remediation:
      - "Improve system prompt: add explicit instructions that the agent MUST use run_code, not just suggest code"
      - "Use models trained for tool use: code-focused models (devstral) may default to explanation over execution"
      - "Modify Archytas agent prompt template in archytas/react.py to emphasize tools MUST be used"

  - id: "3C"
    category: "llm_behavioral"
    name: "Hallucinated / Fabricated Output Data"
    description: |
      When the source data file is not found (FileNotFoundError), some LLMs
      fabricate output data entirely unrelated to the task rather than reporting
      the error and stopping. The fabricated data often matches the model's
      training data patterns (e.g., project management schemas) rather than
      biomedical data.
    severity: "error"
    detection:
      # COMPOUND LOGIC (implemented in Python as _detect_hallucinated_output):
      #   1. metrics.json exists AND column_mapping_accuracy == 0.0
      #   2. extra_columns list contains column names not in GDC schema
      #   3. Often preceded by FileNotFoundError in earlier turns
      log_keywords: []
      log_regex: []
      trace_keywords: []
      trace_regex: []
    example:
      source: "both"
      snippet: |
        // metrics.json showing 0% accuracy with fabricated columns
        {
          "column_mapping_accuracy": 0.0,
          "correct_mappings": 0,
          "total_expected": 11,
          "extra_columns": ["dou_id", "dou_title", "dou_description"]
        }
    remediation:
      - "Fix data path to prevent FileNotFoundError in the first place (see 4A)"
      - "Add data validation: after LLM produces output, verify columns match expected GDC schema"
      - "Add guardrails: check if dou_harmonized.csv contains expected column names before marking run as successful"

  - id: "3D"
    category: "llm_behavioral"
    name: "WebSocket Message Size Exceeded"
    description: |
      The LLM generates a response that exceeds the Beaker WebSocket message
      size limit (4MB default), crashing the connection. Typically happens when
      the model tries to process or output the entire GDC schema at once.
    severity: "error"
    detection:
      log_keywords: []
      log_regex: []
      trace_keywords:
        - "Message size"
        - "exceeds limit"
        - "WebSocketError"
      trace_regex:
        - "Message size \\d+ exceeds limit \\d+"
        - "WebSocketError.*Message size"
    example:
      source: "trace"
      snippet: |
        {
          "status": "error",
          "error_message": "WebSocketError: Message size 5784393 exceeds limit 4194304"
        }
    remediation:
      - "Increase WebSocket limit: set c.ServerApp.websocket_max_message_size = 20 * 1024 * 1024 (20MB) in Jupyter config"
      - "Chunk large data: break large data (full GDC schema) into smaller chunks across multiple turns"
      - "Limit LLM response length: set max_tokens in LLM config (e.g., 4096 tokens per turn)"

  - id: "3E"
    category: "llm_behavioral"
    name: "Context Window Exhaustion (API Token Limit Exceeded)"
    description: |
      The accumulated conversation history (system prompt, all prior turns,
      raw_messages, Beaker state introspection) exceeds the model's maximum
      context length. The LLM provider API rejects the request immediately
      with HTTP 400. Once this occurs, every subsequent turn also fails
      because the conversation history only grows. The error is silently
      swallowed by the archytas/toki layer — agent_response is empty and
      response_type is "llm_response" (not "error"), making the failure
      invisible without raw_messages inspection.

      Distinguishing signature: turns complete in <2 seconds, agent_response
      is empty, and raw_messages stderr contains "maximum context length"
      with an explicit token count. The requested token count is typically
      far above the model's limit (e.g., 1,015,000 vs 200,000).
    severity: "error"
    detection:
      # Keyword detection catches the API error message in serialized trace text.
      # Compound logic (_detect_context_window_exhaustion) cross-checks:
      #   1. Turn has response_type == "llm_response"
      #   2. agent_response is empty ("")
      #   3. duration_seconds < 2.0 (API rejects instantly)
      #   4. raw_messages contain "maximum context length"
      log_keywords: []
      log_regex: []
      trace_keywords:
        - "maximum context length"
      trace_regex:
        - "maximum context length is \\d+ tokens"
        - "you requested about \\d+ tokens"
    example:
      source: "trace"
      snippet: |
        Error from OpenRouter: {'error': {'message': "This endpoint's maximum
        context length is 200000 tokens. However, you requested about 1015152
        tokens (1011709 of text input, 3443 of tool input). Please reduce the
        length of either one, or use the \"middle-out\" transform to compress
        your prompt automatically.", 'code': 400}}
    remediation:
      - "Implement context window monitoring: track approximate token count before each API call and warn at 80% capacity"
      - "Implement conversation summarization or truncation when approaching the model's context limit"
      - "Use provider-specific context compression (e.g., OpenRouter's 'middle-out' transform) if available"
      - "Surface the API error to agent_response instead of silently returning empty"
      - "Reduce Beaker state introspection verbosity: raw_messages include large serialized state objects that inflate context"

  - id: "3F"
    category: "llm_behavioral"
    name: "Response Stream Truncated (Premature Connection Close)"
    description: |
      The LLM provider begins streaming a response but the HTTP connection
      is severed mid-transfer, resulting in a ChunkedEncodingError or
      ProtocolError from urllib3/requests. The archytas/toki layer catches
      the exception but returns an empty string as the agent_response rather
      than raising an error. The turn is recorded as response_type
      "llm_response" (apparent success) with an empty response.

      Distinguishing signature: duration is significant (tens of seconds,
      indicating real LLM processing occurred), agent_response is empty,
      and raw_messages stderr contains "Response ended prematurely" or
      "ChunkedEncodingError". Differs from 3E (context exhaustion) by
      taking real time and having a network-level error rather than a
      token-count error.
    severity: "error"
    detection:
      # Keyword detection catches the network error in serialized trace text.
      # Compound logic (_detect_response_stream_truncated) cross-checks:
      #   1. Turn has response_type == "llm_response"
      #   2. agent_response is empty ("")
      #   3. duration_seconds > 5.0 (real processing occurred before stream broke)
      #   4. raw_messages contain "Response ended prematurely" or "ChunkedEncodingError"
      log_keywords: []
      log_regex: []
      trace_keywords:
        - "Response ended prematurely"
        - "ChunkedEncodingError"
      trace_regex:
        - "(?:Response ended prematurely|ChunkedEncodingError)"
        - "ProtocolError.*Response ended prematurely"
    example:
      source: "trace"
      snippet: |
        LLM Error:
            Response ended prematurely

            Traceback (most recent call last):
              ...
            urllib3.exceptions.ProtocolError: Response ended prematurely

            During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
              ...
            requests.exceptions.ChunkedEncodingError: Response ended prematurely
    remediation:
      - "Implement retry logic for transient network errors (ChunkedEncodingError is typically transient)"
      - "Surface the error in agent_response rather than silently returning empty"
      - "Add response validation: if agent_response is empty after a non-timeout turn, flag as error"
      - "Set request timeout and connection keep-alive parameters in the HTTP client"

  - id: "3G"
    category: "llm_behavioral"
    name: "Silent Empty Response (No Agent Output)"
    description: |
      A turn completes with response_type "llm_response" (apparent success)
      but agent_response is empty or whitespace-only. This is a cross-cutting
      detection that catches any case where the LLM framework silently
      swallowed an error. Specific causes include context window exhaustion
      (3E) and response stream truncation (3F), but this class also catches
      unknown error types that result in empty responses.

      When 3E or 3F is also detected for the same run, 3G provides additional
      context (which specific turns were affected). When neither 3E nor 3F
      is detected, 3G flags an undiagnosed silent failure.
    severity: "warning"
    detection:
      # COMPOUND LOGIC (implemented in Python as _detect_silent_empty_response):
      #   1. Turn has response_type == "llm_response" (not timeout, not error)
      #   2. agent_response is empty or whitespace-only
      #   3. The turn is NOT the last turn (last turn may legitimately be empty)
      # This is purely compound — no keyword/regex patterns.
      log_keywords: []
      log_regex: []
      trace_keywords: []
      trace_regex: []
    example:
      source: "trace"
      snippet: |
        {
          "turn": 4,
          "agent_response": "",
          "response_type": "llm_response",
          "tool_calls": [],
          "duration_seconds": 0.646
        }
    remediation:
      - "Investigate raw_messages for the affected turn to identify the root cause"
      - "Fix the archytas/toki error handling layer to surface errors in agent_response instead of returning empty"
      - "Add response validation in run_experiment.py: abort or retry if agent_response is empty"
      - "Log empty responses as explicit warnings in the experiment output"

  - id: "3H"
    category: "llm_behavioral"
    name: "Ollama Silent Context Truncation (num_ctx Mismatch)"
    description: |
      Ollama silently truncates the input prompt to its default num_ctx=4096
      tokens because Beaker/Archytas does not pass the num_ctx parameter on
      /api/chat calls. The OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH setting in .env is only applied
      during the initial model pre-load (/api/generate), not during subsequent
      chat requests.

      This is a SILENT degradation — Ollama still produces output, but the model
      loses earlier conversation history. The only evidence is a WARN-level log
      line in the Ollama log file. The experiment appears to succeed but output
      quality is degraded because the model lacks context from prior turns.

      Severity ranges from minor (devstral overflows by ~300 tokens, losing a
      small prefix) to catastrophic (qwen3-coder overflows by 688,358 tokens,
      meaning 99.4% of the prompt is discarded).

      Distinguishing signature: Ollama log contains "truncating input prompt"
      with limit=4096 and prompt > 4096. The experiment continues normally
      (no errors in trace.json or SLURM logs).
    severity: "warning"
    detection:
      log_keywords:
        - "truncating input prompt"
      log_regex:
        - "truncating input prompt.*limit=\\d+.*prompt=\\d+"
      trace_keywords: []
      trace_regex: []
    example:
      source: "log"
      snippet: |
        time=2026-02-10T21:08:41.096+01:00 level=WARN source=runner.go:153
        msg="truncating input prompt" limit=4096 prompt=4200 keep=5 new=4096
    remediation:
      - "Pass num_ctx in every /api/chat call: modify the Archytas Ollama model adapter to include num_ctx in request options"
      - "Set OLLAMA_NUM_CTX=64000 as an Ollama server environment variable (applies globally to all /api/chat calls)"
      - "Bake num_ctx into the Modelfile: add 'PARAMETER num_ctx 64000' to each model's Modelfile"
      - "Add Ollama log monitoring: parse Ollama logs for 'truncating input prompt' warnings and flag in experiment results"

  # ===========================================================================
  # Category 4: Data / Configuration Path Errors
  # ===========================================================================

  - id: "4A"
    category: "data_path"
    name: "FileNotFoundError — Incorrect Data Path in Container"
    description: |
      The LLM (or the code it generates) tries to access a file path that does
      not exist inside the container. Causes include: incorrect path in config
      YAML (e.g., /data/... instead of data/...), Beaker kernel cwd not set to
      /workspace, or LLM generating an absolute path that doesn't match the
      container's mount structure.
    severity: "error"
    detection:
      log_keywords: []
      log_regex: []
      trace_keywords:
        - "FileNotFoundError"
        - "No such file or directory"
      trace_regex:
        - "FileNotFoundError.*No such file or directory"
        - "\\[Errno 2\\].*No such file or directory"
    example:
      source: "trace"
      snippet: |
        {
          "content": {
            "ename": "FileNotFoundError",
            "evalue": "[Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'data/one_metadata_table_gdc_schema/data/dou.csv'",
            "execution_type": "tool",
            "execution_item_name": "run_code"
          }
        }
    remediation:
      - "Use absolute paths in configs: /workspace/data/one_metadata_table_gdc_schema/data/dou.csv"
      - "Fix kernel working directory: ensure Beaker kernel starts with cwd set to /workspace"
      - "Restructure workspace with symlinks: mount data as symlinks directly in workspace root"

  # ===========================================================================
  # Category 5: Missing / Incorrect Output
  # ===========================================================================

  - id: "5A"
    category: "output"
    name: "No Output Produced"
    description: |
      The experiment completes (or times out) without producing dou_harmonized.csv
      or any mapping files in the results directory. Results directory exists but
      contains only trace.json and possibly metrics.json. Almost always a downstream
      effect of another failure category (1-4).
    severity: "warning"
    detection:
      # COMPOUND LOGIC (implemented in Python as _detect_no_output):
      #   1. Results directory exists
      #   2. trace.json exists
      #   3. No dou_harmonized.csv in results directory
      #   4. No column_mapping.json or value_mapping.json
      # This is checked by examining the results folder contents, not by
      # keyword/regex matching.
      log_keywords: []
      log_regex: []
      trace_keywords: []
      trace_regex: []
    example:
      source: "both"
      snippet: |
        Results directory contains only:
          trace.json
          metrics.json
        Missing expected files:
          dou_harmonized.csv
          column_mapping.json
          value_mapping.json
    remediation:
      - "Fix upstream issues first: this is almost always a downstream effect of another failure"
      - "Add output verification: after final turn, check if expected output files exist; log NO_OUTPUT_PRODUCED status"
      - "Add save results fallback: if LLM produced intermediate results in memory, add automated save step"

  # ===========================================================================
  # Category 6: Diagnostic / Informational
  # ===========================================================================

  - id: "6A"
    category: "diagnostic"
    name: "Kernel State Budget Enforced"
    description: |
      The kernel state budget enforcement dropped one or more variables
      from the serialized state sent to the LLM. This is informational —
      it means the budget system is working as intended and prevented a
      potential context window explosion.

      The _budget_metadata object in the auto-context shows what was dropped
      and why. Common scenarios:
        - BDI schema objects (SchemaGraph, SimilarityFloodingMatcher) blacklisted
        - Large intermediate variables dropped due to per-variable size cap
        - Variables dropped because total budget was exceeded
        - Unchanged variables sent as compact summaries (delta tracking)

      If important variables were dropped, they should be added to the
      var_whitelist in the experiment YAML's context_management section.
    severity: "info"
    detection:
      log_keywords: []
      log_regex: []
      trace_keywords:
        - "_budget_metadata"
        - "dropped_count"
      trace_regex:
        - "\"dropped_count\":\\s*[1-9]"
    example:
      source: "trace"
      snippet: |
        {
          "_budget_metadata": {
            "dropped_count": 3,
            "unchanged_count": 5,
            "budget_total": 64000,
            "max_var_size": 20000,
            "final_size_chars": 42150
          }
        }
    remediation:
      - "Informational only: the budget system prevented a context explosion"
      - "If important variables were dropped, add them to var_whitelist in experiment YAML context_management.python_kernel section"
      - "If too many variables are dropped, increase state_budget_pct or max_variable_size in context_management.python_kernel"
      - "Use the log analysis CLI tool with --verbose to see which specific variables were affected"

# Harmonia Project Instructions

## Before Starting Any Task

1. **Read latest instructions**: `harmonia_metadata_agent/analysis/dstoker/harmonia/my_instructions/` (most recent by date)
2. **Ask user** if instructions are still current or if anything has changed
3. **Check datasets**: `harmonia_metadata_agent/raw/datasets_harmonia/` for experiment data

## After Code Changes

Always look at harmonia_metadata_agent/analysis/dstoker/harmonia/documentation/codebase_descriptions; find the latest .md file, see if what you have just implemented necessitates changes to this description. If so: generate the diffs needed to this file. Then, if the file has the correct date (check with Bash(date +%d_%m_%Y)) edit that file. Otherwise, generate a new one with the same file name convention and correct date.

## After Experiment Runs (Log Auditing)

Use the log/trace analysis CLI tool to audit experiment results:

```bash
cd harmonia_metadata_agent/analysis/dstoker/harmonia
.venv/bin/python code_development_tools_agents/monitoring_and_evaluation/read_and_analyze_logs_and_traces_cli.py
```

This detects 13 categories of failure modes (infrastructure hangs, model not found, API errors, LLM behavioral issues, missing output, etc.) by analyzing both SLURM logs and trace.json files. Use `--verbose` for per-turn analysis, `--json` for machine-readable output, or `--run-id <id>` / `--experiment <name>` to filter.

The error taxonomy is defined in `code_development_tools_agents/monitoring_and_evaluation/types_of_log_and_trace_problems.yaml`. The human-readable failure mode reference is in `documentation/processes/11_02_2026_interpreting_logs_and_traces.md`.

## Project Overview

**Goal:** Run metadata harmonization agents using LLMs + Beaker to evaluate performance on biomedical data harmonization tasks.

**Full documentation:** `harmonia_metadata_agent/analysis/dstoker/harmonia/documentation/codebase_descriptions/` (read the latest by date)

## Key Paths

| Resource | Path |
|----------|------|
| Source code | `harmonia_metadata_agent/analysis/dstoker/harmonia/src/` |
| Experiment configs | `harmonia_metadata_agent/analysis/dstoker/harmonia/experiments/experiment_1_harmonia_dou2020_gdc/configs/automated/` |
| Datasets | `harmonia_metadata_agent/raw/datasets_harmonia/` |
| Gold standard | `harmonia_metadata_agent/raw/datasets_harmonia/one_metadata_table_gdc_schema/gold_standard/` |
| Results | `harmonia_metadata_agent/analysis/dstoker/harmonia/results/` |
| Logs | `harmonia_metadata_agent/analysis/dstoker/harmonia/logs/` |
| Evaluation code | `harmonia_metadata_agent/analysis/dstoker/harmonia/src/evaluation/` |
| Log analysis tool | `harmonia_metadata_agent/analysis/dstoker/harmonia/code_development_tools_agents/monitoring_and_evaluation/` |
| Failure mode docs | `harmonia_metadata_agent/analysis/dstoker/harmonia/documentation/processes/` |
| Apptainer image | `harmonia_metadata_agent/analysis/dstoker/harmonia/harmonia_beaker_LLM_agent_environment_apptainer.sif` |
| Python venv | `harmonia_metadata_agent/analysis/dstoker/harmonia/.venv/` |
| Model registries | `harmonia_metadata_agent/analysis/dstoker/harmonia/LLM_associated_metadata/` |

## Current State

- **Working:** Automated experiments with multiple LLM backends, manual interactive experiments
- **Working:** Metrics evaluation pipeline (`src/evaluation/`) comparing harmonized output to gold standard
- **Working:** Log/trace analysis CLI tool for diagnosing experiment failures
- **Working:** Per-job Ollama isolation (dynamic ports, per-job PID/runtime dirs)
- **Working:** Uniform experiment tracking via 8-char hex run IDs linking logs to results

## Experiment Types

1. **Automated:** Scripted interactions in `configs/automated/*.yaml` - same script runs for each LLM
2. **Manual:** Interactive Beaker notebook via port forwarding (configure LLM in `.env`)

## Running Experiments

### Manual interactive experiments (ALWAYS use --monitor)

When the user asks to start a manual/interactive experiment, **always use `--monitor`** so that
`conversation.md` and `trace.json` are produced. Without `--monitor`, Beaker runs but nothing
is logged.

```bash
# Cloud LLM providers
srun --time=04:00:00 --mem=10G \
    ./exec_apptainer_harmonia.sh --config <manual_config.yaml> --monitor

# Local LLM providers (ALWAYS use GPU partition!)
srun --partition=gpu --gpus-per-node=1 --time=04:00:00 --mem=64G --cpus-per-task=8 \
    ./exec_apptainer_harmonia.sh --config <manual_config.yaml> --monitor
```

The `--monitor` flag starts Beaker in the background and launches a WebSocket monitor
(`run_manual_experiment.py`) that passively captures all user/agent interactions into
`results/<experiment_name>_<timestamp>_<run_id>/trace.json` and `conversation.md`.

### Automated experiments

```bash
# Start Beaker server first (cloud)
./exec_apptainer_harmonia.sh --config <config.yaml>

# Start Beaker server first (local LLM — ALWAYS use GPU partition!)
srun --partition=gpu --gpus-per-node=1 --time=04:00:00 --mem=64G --cpus-per-task=8 \
    ./exec_apptainer_harmonia.sh --config <config.yaml>

# Then run the automated experiment script
python run_experiment.py <config.yaml>
```

## IMPORTANT: Local LLM Jobs

**Always use GPU partition for local LLM providers** (ollama, anyllm:ollama, local, anyllm:local).
Loading models on CPU takes 10-15+ minutes vs seconds on GPU. Without GPU:
- Model loading is extremely slow
- Inference is impractically slow
- Jobs may timeout before completing

When starting interactive sessions with local LLMs, ALWAYS include:
- `--partition=gpu`
- `--gpus-per-node=1`

**Startup timing:** After starting Ollama, wait at least 2.5 minutes before checking if Beaker is ready - model pre-loading takes time.

---

## Verification Protocol for Capability Claims

**Before claiming any functionality is unavailable:**

1. **Define 3+ test methods** - Direct API call, documentation check, working examples
2. **Search documentation** - Use WebSearch with targeted keywords
3. **Execute tests** - Run each method, document actual results
4. **Report with evidence** - "Tested via [methods]. Result: [outcome]"

**Never claim unavailability based on:** missing documentation alone, single failed attempt, assumptions about similar versions

---

## Python Environment

**Always use the project `.venv`**, not conda or system Python:

```bash
cd harmonia_metadata_agent/analysis/dstoker/harmonia
.venv/bin/python <script.py>
```

This venv has Python 3.11, pydantic 2.12.5, PyYAML, and other project dependencies. Do NOT probe for conda environments or try `module load` — just use `.venv`.

---

## Model Registry Management

Before generating configs for OpenRouter models, check if the registry is current:
```bash
cd harmonia_metadata_agent/analysis/dstoker/harmonia
# Check age of registry file
find LLM_associated_metadata/openrouter_models.json -mmin +1440 2>/dev/null && echo "STALE" || echo "FRESH"
# If stale or missing (fetches both models and parameter meanings):
.venv/bin/python LLM_associated_metadata/fetch_openrouter.py
```

For Ollama models:
```bash
find LLM_associated_metadata/ollama_models.json -mmin +1440 2>/dev/null && echo "STALE" || echo "FRESH"
# If stale or missing:
.venv/bin/python LLM_associated_metadata/fetch_ollama_models.py
```

When creating configs for specific models, use `lookup_model.py` to get accurate metadata:
```bash
.venv/bin/python LLM_associated_metadata/lookup_model.py config-snippet openrouter:<model-id>
```

The `manage_configs.py clone` command auto-enriches configs with `model_metadata` from the registry (pricing, context length, capabilities). If the registry is stale or missing, it prints a warning.

---

## Practical Lessons

- **`.gitignore` uses repo-relative paths.** Absolute paths (e.g., `/hpc/compgen/.../logs/*`) silently fail. Use `logs/` not `/hpc/.../logs/*`.
- **`logs/` and `results/` are gitignored.** They contain experiment output (trace.json, conversation.md, SLURM logs) that should not be version-controlled.
- **Run IDs link logs to results.** Every experiment gets an 8-char hex ID. In automated mode, the SBATCH template generates it; in manual mode, `exec_apptainer_harmonia.sh` generates it. The ID appears in log filenames, results directory names, and the `.experiment_id` JSON file.
- **Gold standard files live outside the git repo** in `harmonia_metadata_agent/raw/datasets_harmonia/.../gold_standard/`. They are referenced by absolute path in experiment config YAMLs.

# Proposed Commit Message

```
Add experiment tracking, metrics evaluation, per-job Ollama isolation,
log analysis tooling, and automated experiment infrastructure overhaul

This commit represents the work from 05-Feb through 11-Feb 2026 across
multiple sessions. It touches nearly every layer of the Harmonia
experiment automation stack: infrastructure scripts, automation
framework, experiment configs, evaluation pipeline, and developer
tooling.

---

## 1. Metrics Evaluation Pipeline (NEW)

Added `src/evaluation/` with Pydantic v2 schema (v1.1) and metrics
calculation for comparing LLM-harmonized output to gold standard data.

- `src/evaluation/schemas.py` — Pydantic models: ExperimentMetadata,
  ColumnMappingMetrics (dual precision incl/excl null), ColumnValueMetrics
  (per-column accuracy, macro-averaged P/R/F1), ErrorCategorization
  (whitespace_only, case_only, genuine), confusion matrices, OverallSummary
- `src/evaluation/metrics.py` — Core calculation: column mapping quality,
  value harmonization quality, numeric tolerance for float columns,
  index-based row alignment (inner join), error categorization
- `calculate_metrics.py` — Standalone CLI entry point for metrics
  calculation against gold standard CSVs

Metrics are also auto-calculated at the end of `run_experiment.py` when
an `evaluation:` block is present in the experiment config YAML.

See: plans/10_02_2026_implementing_metadata_harmonization_metrics_calculation.md

## 2. Evaluation Config Support in Experiment YAMLs

- `src/automation/config.py` — Added EvaluationConfig dataclass with
  fields for gold_standard, gold_column_mapping, gold_value_mapping,
  acceptable_columns_file, column/value mapping file names,
  index_column, and numeric_tolerance. Wired into ExperimentConfig
  and from_dict() parser.
- Created gold standard reference files for Experiment 1 (dou.csv)
  in raw/datasets_harmonia/one_metadata_table_gdc_schema/gold_standard/:
  - harmonized_dou_correct.csv — manually verified harmonized output
  - gold_standard_column_mapping.json — correct source→GDC column map
  - gold_standard_value_mapping.json — correct value transformations
  - harmonization_acceptable_columns.json — acceptable column alternatives
  (These files live outside this repo in the shared raw/ directory.)
- All automated experiment configs updated with `evaluation:` blocks
  pointing to those gold standard files
- `run_experiment.py` — Added post-experiment metrics calculation:
  loads gold standard, runs calculate_all_metrics(), writes metrics.json

## 3. Uniform Experiment Tracking with Run ID (NEW)

Every experiment run is now assigned a unique 8-char hex run ID
(secrets.token_hex(4)) that links SLURM logs to results folders.

- `sbatch_template.sh`, `sbatch_template_gpu.sh` — Generate RUN_ID
  before log redirect; include in log filenames
  (logs/<timestamp>_<name>_<jobid>_<run_id>.out); pass --run-id to
  exec script
- `exec_apptainer_harmonia.sh` — Added --run-id/-R flag; auto-generates
  RUN_ID if not provided; includes run_id in results directory name;
  creates .experiment_id JSON metadata file in results directory
- `src/automation/runner.py` — Reads RUN_ID from os.environ; includes
  in output directory name

The .experiment_id file contains: run_id, experiment_name,
experiment_mode (automated/manual), config_file, llm_provider,
llm_model, timestamp, slurm_job_id, and log_files paths.

See: plans/11_02_2026_1250_implementation_spec_uniform_experiment_tracking_with_unique_ID.md

## 4. Per-Job Ollama Isolation

- `exec_apptainer_harmonia.sh` — Major rewrite (~630 lines added):
  dynamic Ollama port per SLURM job (11434 + 1 + SLURM_JOB_ID % 200),
  per-job PID file (.ollama_${SLURM_JOB_ID}.pid), per-job runtime
  directory ($TMPDIR/ollama_${SLURM_JOB_ID}), per-job serve log,
  automatic Ollama start/stop for local LLM providers, model
  pre-loading/warming, proper cleanup on exit
- `sbatch_template_gpu.sh` — Displays Ollama port in job output
- Interactive/manual mode (no SLURM) keeps default port 11434

See: plans/10_02_2026_1830_make_separate_ollama_instances.md

## 5. Log and Trace Analysis Tooling (NEW)

- `code_development_tools_agents/monitoring_and_evaluation/
  types_of_log_and_trace_problems.yaml` — Machine-readable error
  taxonomy with 13 problem classes across 5 categories:
  Infrastructure (1A), LLM Connectivity (2A-2D), LLM Behavior (3A-3C),
  Data/Config (4A-4B), Experiment Lifecycle (5A-5C). Each class has
  detection keywords, regex patterns, severity, examples, remediation.
- `code_development_tools_agents/monitoring_and_evaluation/
  read_and_analyze_logs_and_traces_cli.py` — CLI tool (~700 lines)
  with Pydantic output schema. Discovers logs and results directories,
  links them by run_id (new) or experiment_name+timestamp (legacy),
  detects problems via keyword matching AND compound Python logic
  (e.g., distinguishing "all turns timed out" infrastructure hang
  from "some turns timed out" LLM-side timeout). Supports --verbose,
  --json, --run-id, --experiment filtering.
- `documentation/processes/11_02_2026_interpreting_logs_and_traces.md`
  — Comprehensive human-readable failure mode reference document

See: plans/11_02_2026_1140_analyze_failure_modes_automated_experiments.md

## 6. Manual Experiment Monitoring

- `run_manual_experiment.py` — Major expansion: WebSocket passive
  monitoring of interactive Beaker sessions, producing trace.json
  and conversation.md just like automated experiments. Supports
  --monitor flag via exec_apptainer_harmonia.sh for single-command
  launch.
- `src/automation/manual_runner.py` — ManualExperimentRunner class
  for passive WebSocket monitoring with auto-save after each turn.

## 7. SBATCH Templates & Log Naming

- Both templates now use date-stamped log filenames:
  logs/<DD-MM-YYYY_HHMM>_<experiment_name>_<SLURM_JOB_ID>_<run_id>.out
  (previously: logs/<experiment_name>_<jobid>.out)
- GPU template adds --gpus-per-node=1 and --partition=gpu
- Both pass --run-id and --job-name to exec_apptainer_harmonia.sh

## 8. Experiment Config Changes

- DELETED: dou_harmonization_mimo-v2-flash.yaml (and _associated.env)
  — OpenRouter free period ended, model no longer available
- DELETED: dou_harmonization_anyllm_openrouter.yaml (and _associated.env)
  — Same reason (used mimo-v2-flash via anyllm:openrouter)
- MODIFIED: dou_harmonization_olmo3.yaml — Changed model from
  olmo-3.1:32b to olmo-3:32b-think (correct Ollama registry name)
- All configs: Added evaluation: block with gold standard paths,
  added data path prefix fix (data/ -> data/one_metadata_table...)

## 9. Container & Build

- `harmonia_beaker_LLM_agent_environment_apptainer.def` (NEW) —
  Apptainer definition with any-llm-sdk, ollama package
- `build_harmonia_apptainer.sh` (NEW) — Build script for new image

## 10. .gitignore & Housekeeping

- Fixed .gitignore: replaced non-functional absolute path with
  relative `logs/` and `results/` entries
- Removed 58 log files and 59 results files from git tracking
  (files remain on disk, just untracked going forward)
- Added `src/evaluation/`, `code_development_tools_agents/`,
  documentation, plans, instructions as new tracked directories

## 11. Documentation

- `documentation/codebase_descriptions/how_this_codebase_works_11_02_2026.md`
  — Updated codebase description with all changes above
- `documentation/codebase_descriptions/how_this_codebase_works_10_02_2026.md`
  — Previous day's description
- `documentation/codebase_descriptions/how_this_codebase_works_05_02_2026.md`
  — Earlier description (any-llm integration)

---

For detailed context on each feature area, see:
- plans/11_02_2026_1250_implementation_spec_uniform_experiment_tracking_with_unique_ID.md
- plans/11_02_2026_1140_analyze_failure_modes_automated_experiments.md
- plans/10_02_2026_1830_make_separate_ollama_instances.md
- plans/10_02_2026_implementing_metadata_harmonization_metrics_calculation.md
- documentation/processes/11_02_2026_interpreting_logs_and_traces.md

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
```
